concerns.text: The 'neural (non-physics) teacher signal' for the baseline is never defined. Where does it come from — a separately trained neural model? A pretrained video predictor? Without specifying how the neural teacher is produced, the core contrast (physics vs neural teacher) has no operationalized second arm, and the baseline cannot be implemented or interpreted. Construct validity of the entire comparison depends on this.

concerns.location: plan.md: T4.3 / research.md 'FID computed on CPU with torchmetrics'
concerns.text: FID between physics-teacher-generated and neural-teacher-baseline video sets is statistically meaningless at the planned scale. FID requires thousands of samples for stable estimates; with a test set sized for a paired t-test (tens of sequences, 16 frames each), FID will be dominated by estimator bias. The plan's power analysis (T4.0) covers only the t-test, not FID. Either justify the sample size for FID or downgrade FID to a descriptive, non-inferential metric with an explicit small-sample caveat.

Ablation uses 3 values per parameter (friction 0.2/0.5/0.8, elasticity 0.1/0.5/0.9). A linear regression / Pearson r on 3 points has ~1 df and essentially no power; SC-006's p-values will be uninterpretable. Specify more parameter levels or per-level replicates so the regression has adequate df, or state that the ablation is descriptive only.

Paired t-test on sequence-level SSIM/LPIPS assumes approximate normality of paired differences; no check (e.g. Shapiro–Wilk) or non-parametric fallback (Wilcoxon signed-rank) is planned. Add a normality check or fallback so SC-004's significance decisions are defensible.

FR-007 requires the neural-teacher baseline to be trained 'on the original Causal Forcing++ dataset', but the plan (Scope Note, T2.1) substitutes the same synthetic physics dataset because no verified source for the original dataset exists. The plan correctly flags the gap, but the spec FR-007 remains unamended, so the plan element has no matching FR as written. The spec must be revised (e.g., FR-007 reworded to 'on a shared, verified dataset isolating the teacher-type comparison, with the original-dataset arm noted as unavailable') so the plan and spec agree; otherwise FR-007 is unbacked as literally stated.

concerns.location: research.md: Dataset Strategy table, row 'Physics Engine Metadata (seed, world definition)'
concerns.text: The only external dataset cited is a BipedalWalker-v3 RL expert-trajectory metadata.json (frankcholula/Box2D). That file contains Gym/Gymnasium episode metadata for an RL control task — it does not provide 'world parameters' or initial-state vectors suitable for instantiating the plan's deterministic Box2D rigid-body video simulations (friction/elasticity sweeps, rendered 16-frame sequences). The URL reaches, but the dataset is the wrong one for this use. Either drop the external download entirely (the plan already generates worlds from a pinned seed, so it is not needed) or cite a source that actually defines Box2D world definitions compatible with the generate.py pipeline.

Plan T2.1 trains the neural-teacher baseline on the synthetic physics dataset, but spec FR-007 (unchanged) mandates 'the original Causal Forcing++ dataset'. The plan transparently flags the gap, but until spec.md FR-007/SC-008 are revised to match, plan and spec contradict each other and downstream stages cannot verify FR-007 as written. Revise the spec (or obtain FR-007 waiver) in the same change set.

Plan header and Project Structure place all design docs under 'specs/002-llmxive-physics-teacher-distillation/', but the actual artifacts (plan.md, research.md, data-model.md, contracts/*) live under 'specs/001-llmxive-follow-up-extending-causal-forci/'. Relative links (e.g. '../specs/002-.../spec.md') will not resolve. Align directory naming.

Schema enum is ['physics_teacher','neural_teacher'], but the plan's evaluated models are the 'student model' (trained on the physics-teacher signal) and the 'neural-teacher baseline'. No plan task produces predictions from a model literally named 'physics_teacher'. Rename the enum value (e.g. 'student_physics_teacher') or state the mapping explicitly so T4.1–T7.1 outputs validate.

Trajectory-Pixel Correlation (T4.1–T4.4, outputs/metrics/trajectory_pixel_corr.csv) has no corresponding entity or field in data-model.md or any contract; the data model defines only PhysicsTrajectory, VideoSequence, EvaluationResults. Add the metric output to the data model or an additional_info field mapping.

concerns.location: plan.md: Phase 4 / T4.4 and research.md 'Teacher‑Signal Quality Metric'
concerns.text: Trajectory‑Pixel Correlation (Pearson r between physics velocities and optical flow of the rendered frames) is circular: the frames are rendered deterministically FROM the physics trajectory, so pixel motion is a known function of the velocities. The correlation can only 'confirm' the renderer works; it is not an empirical measure of 'teacher-signal quality'. Relabel it as a rendering-pipeline sanity check, or compute it on STUDENT-generated frames (where it becomes a genuine, falsifiable fidelity measure of motion).

concerns.location: plan.md: T2.1 / Scope Note; research.md 'Neural‑teacher baseline on the same physics data'
concerns.text: The 'neural (non-physics) teacher signal' is never defined. If the neural teacher is itself trained on the same synthetic physics data, its signal derives from the same ground truth as the physics teacher, weakening the claimed 'teacher-type' contrast and risking a near-tautological comparison. Specify what the neural teacher is (architecture, target, training data) and acknowledge that both arms share the same information source, limiting the inference to 'analytic vs learned encoding of the same signal'.

FID is computed between two MODEL-OUTPUT sets (physics-teacher videos vs neural-teacher baseline videos), not against real data or ground truth. Interpreting 'lower FID = higher generative richness' is not valid in that configuration — FID between two generated sets measures distributional similarity, not richness. Restate the interpretation (e.g., similarity to baseline distribution) or add an FID against ground-truth frames.

new_concerns.text: Plan T2.1 still trains the neural‑teacher baseline on the synthetic physics dataset, which directly conflicts with FR‑007 that mandates training on the original Causal Forcing++ dataset. The spec has not been revised to accommodate this gap, so the plan and spec remain contradictory.

The plan evaluates the deterministic physics‑teacher model directly against ground‑truth frames using SSIM, PSNR, and LPIPS. Because the physics teacher’s outputs are the ground‑truth renderings, these metrics will be perfect (SSIM = 1, PSNR = ∞, LPIPS = 0), making the paired statistical tests trivial and not a valid test of the core hypothesis that a physics teacher can replace a neural teacher for distillation. The evaluation should instead compare *student* models trained with each teacher (physics‑teacher‑distilled vs neural‑teacher‑distilled) on the held‑out test set, using the same fidelity metrics, to assess whether the physics teacher provides a useful learning signal.
